Zimbabwe Real Estate Sector Faces Disruptions Amidst Nationwide Workers' Walkout

Zimbabwe’s real estate sector is experiencing significant disruptions as thousands of property management staff, estate agents, and administrative employees staged a coordinated walkout on Wednesday, demanding higher wages and improved working conditions. The action, led by the Zimbabwe Real Estate Workers’ Union, has brought operations to a standstill at many of the country’s major agencies and property management firms.

Offices in Harare, Bulawayo, and Mutare have seen staff absenteeism rates exceeding 80%, according to industry estimates. Property viewings, lease signings, and site inspections have been postponed or cancelled, leaving tenants and landlords in limbo. With many agency branches shuttered or operating with skeletal staff, the processing of rental agreements and property sales has slowed dramatically.

A spokesperson for the Zimbabwe Real Estate Federation, the industry’s main trade association, stated, “The walkout has severely impacted our members’ ability to serve clients and manage ongoing projects. We are urging both parties to return to the negotiating table as soon as possible.” Several firms, including UrbanEdge Realty and PrimeCity Properties, have issued statements acknowledging delays in client services and citing uncertainty over when normal operations will resume.

Workers are calling for a 60% wage increase, citing the rising cost of living and currency instability. “Our salaries have not kept pace with inflation. We are struggling to make ends meet while property values soar,” said Tapiwa Moyo, a negotiator for the striking workers. Union leaders report that discussions with the Zimbabwe Real Estate Employers’ Association have stalled, prompting the industry-wide action.

Industry analysts warn that a prolonged strike could create a backlog in property transactions and disrupt ongoing site management activities. As the strike enters its third day, both employers and workers remain at an impasse, with no immediate resolution in sight.
